chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Cat Anderson's high C's and his teacher
summary: McRae says Cat Anderson's non-pressure study with a teacher let him hit five C's, which no one on television bands could match.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Just like the trumpet -- the teacher that Cat Anderson studied with. The guy told Cat Anderson, "You stay with me, I'll make you the greatest trumpet player in the business." And he did.
I say, "Cat stayed with that man." He was teaching him non-pressure. When Cat come out, he could hit the 5 C's. You hear them all.
He say, "Now, I'm gonna hit all five for you." And that last one was up there, and I ain't heard no white boy play a note that big.
And I heard Maynard Ferguson, he's screaming with his little peewee note there. And Cat would hit a note, hit a C --
He had to change mouthpieces to go that high. Cat ain't change no mouthpiece. It's the same mouthpiece.
He did (singing notes), hit all five of them. The band say, yoom. On the end, he be out there by himself and the band would break off, and Cat would say -- hit them C's (singing notes). Then he

start (singing notes), last one. You hear that last one -- the last C on that horn you could -- he couldn't go no higher. Pop it just like a (inaudible). And the band come in, yoom! People go crazy. You haven't heard -- you haven't seen -- You name me one cat -- one trumpet player living today who could what Cat Anderson did. That man turned him out. There's no trumpet player living today right now I could name that could hit those C's -- hit those five C's like Cat Anderson. Even the boy that's got the band with Johnny Carson. He's a good trumpet player. But none of those boys didn't come up to Cat.
What the boy, a trumpet player that --
Doc Severinson can't play what Cat and them boys played -- Cat and them played. You got guys in Basie's band. You ain't

hear nobody in that band that could hit them C's. You have to be taught that. And very few of them guys that spent that money.
Cat spent money -- That man didn't charge him no two dollars to (inaudible). Cat paid good money to stay with that man.
And every time he came in town, he was right there. If he was in town for a week, he studied with that man every other day. He'd go down, (work out, work out, (inaudible)) work out.
